package.name: ingest
package.packageFile:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/package.schema.json

# INGEST, migrating one node at a time.
#
# Abyssale is the first. The other three are still TypeScript and each is blocked on something
# different, which is worth writing down because the package name suggests otherwise — "ingest REST
# nodes" was on the backlog as ready, and reading them proved it wrong:
#
#   PlaidTransactions  MIGRATED 2026-07-28 needing NO new capability, which is not what this note said a
#                      day earlier. All three of its supposed blockers dissolved once the vendor API was
#                      read rather than the old code.
#   GoogleSheet        MIGRATED as a REWRITE: it was a Sheets client AND a loop in one node, holding rows
#                      in actor state. It returns every row now and LoopStart/LoopEnd iterate.
#   DocumentParser     RETIRED and REPLACED by unstructured/ParseDocument. It parsed pdf/docx in process
#                      with `pdf-parse` and `mammoth`, which no manifest can express — and did not need
#                      to, once one HTTP call covered the same job and twenty more formats.
#   Document           RETIRED with no replacement: it existed to feed DocumentParser, and every metadata
#                      field it emitted came from its own input.
#   SpatialIngest      MIGRATED 2026-07-28 by DELETING the pipeline rather than describing it. It had
#                      reimplemented the content engine — 373 lines, 220 of them a drifted COPY of the
#                      engine's extraction prompts and schemas, with its own embedding call and its own
#                      write to the dictionary. The engine's MANUAL connector was written for this node
#                      and never used. Now it hands raw text over and the engine does the rest.

name: ingest
displayName: Ingest
description: Content ingestion, template rendering and data import
version: 2.1.0
category: ingest
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

features:
  - Render branded images and PDFs from Abyssale templates
  - Fetch realistic test bank transactions from Plaid Sandbox
  - Read rows from a public Google Sheet

allowedHosts:
  # LOOPBACK, numeric form (the pattern rejects a bare "localhost"): SpatialIngest hands its
  # text to the platform's own content engine over `scope.engineUrl` (127.0.0.1:4101), same
  # declaration the spatial package carries for its searches.
  - 127.0.0.1
  - api.abyssale.com
  # Plaid picks its host from the credential's environment, so all three are declared. A sandbox key
  # cannot reach production and vice versa, so listing them is not a widening.
  - sheets.googleapis.com
  - sandbox.plaid.com
  - development.plaid.com
  - production.plaid.com

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.5.0"
  # apiKeyHeader for Abyssale (x-api-key), apiKeyQuery for Google Sheets (?key=). Plaid needs
  # neither: it authenticates in the request BODY, so it declares no scheme at all.
  credential: [apiKeyHeader, apiKeyQuery]
  transport: [json]
  # Abyssale generation is asynchronous: POST to start, then ask the generation request until it is
  # finalized. Without `poll` the node would settle on the RECEIPT — a request id — and emit that as
  # the finished asset, with nothing reporting a problem.
  poll: true

credentials.abyssaleCredential.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/credential.schema.json

name: abyssaleCredential
displayName: Abyssale
description: Abyssale API credentials for high-quality template rendering

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Abyssale API key from the dashboard
    placeholder: Enter your Abyssale API key
credentials.googleApiCredential.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/credential.schema.json

# MOVED HERE, not copied, and moved NOW even though GoogleSheet is still TypeScript.
#
# Credential declaration is all-or-nothing per package: `registerCredentialType` is
# first-wins-and-SILENT, so a credentials/*.yaml alongside a live `api.registerCredential()` means
# whichever loads first takes the slot and the other vanishes — surfacing later as an auth failure
# with the right credential visibly selected. Migrating ONE node therefore moves EVERY credential the
# package declares.
#
# Nothing breaks for the code nodes: the type registry is shared, so GoogleSheet reads
# `googleApiCredential` exactly as before. Only the source of the declaration changed.

name: googleApiCredential
displayName: Google API
description: Google API credentials for accessing Google services

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Google API key with Sheets API enabled
    placeholder: Enter your Google API key
credentials.plaidCredential.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/credential.schema.json

# Moved with the others — see googleApiCredential.yaml for why declaration is all-or-nothing.

name: plaidCredential
displayName: Plaid
description: Plaid API credentials for accessing banking data (Sandbox/Development/Production)

properties:
  - name: clientId
    displayName: Client ID
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: false
    description: Your Plaid client ID from the Plaid Dashboard
    placeholder: Enter your Plaid client ID
  - name: secret
    displayName: Secret
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Plaid secret key (use Sandbox secret for testing)
    placeholder: Enter your Plaid secret
  - name: environment
    displayName: Environment
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: "Plaid environment: sandbox, development, or production"
    placeholder: sandbox
    default: sandbox

files.api/events.yaml:
# `response` is the FINAL transactions reply — the one the poll settled on, not the sandbox login.
#
# `startDate` and `endDate` are recomputed here rather than read off the reply. Plaid does not echo the
# range back, and the two rows use the SAME expressions the request body used, so what a workflow reads
# is exactly what was asked for.

- emit: transactions
  value: "return response.transactions || []"

- emit: accounts
  value: "return response.accounts || []"

- emit: totalTransactions
  # `total_transactions` is how many EXIST, which is not the same as how many came back — `count`
  # caps the page. The existing node emitted the total, so this does too.
  value: "return response.total_transactions || 0"

- emit: startDate
  value: "return Date.iso(Date.now() - (config.daysBack || 30) * 86400000).split('T')[0]"

- emit: endDate
  value: "return Date.iso().split('T')[0]"
files.api/run.yaml:
# THREE CALLS, and all three exist because this node MANUFACTURES ITS OWN TEST LOGIN.
#
# It is a sandbox data source by design, never a live one: it creates a pretend bank connection, turns
# that into an access token, and reads made-up transactions from it. A real account would need a token
# that only exists after a person logs into their bank through Plaid's browser popup, which a workflow
# node cannot do. Two of these three calls are that pretence; only the last one fetches anything.
#
# NO `auth` BLOCK ANYWHERE, and that is not an omission. Plaid authenticates in the BODY — every
# request repeats client_id and secret — so there is no header for a scheme to set.
#
# THE URL IS AN EXPRESSION, not a template, because `environment` is an OPTIONAL credential field
# defaulting to sandbox. Templated as "https://{{ … }}.plaid.com" an unset value yields
# "https://.plaid.com", which resolves to nothing and fails as a DNS error naming no cause. The
# fallback has to live where the url is built.
#
# NOTHING NEW WAS NEEDED FOR THIS NODE, which was not true a day ago. It looked blocked on three
# capabilities and needed none of them:
#
#   the YYYY-MM-DD date range   `Date.iso` formats a timestamp, so the range is computed inline
#   the PRODUCT_NOT_READY wait  that IS polling — ask again until ready — see the last call
#   the Redis cache             dropped; see the note in node.yaml

- name: login
  method: POST
  url: "return 'https://' + (credentials.plaidCredential.environment || 'sandbox') + '.plaid.com/sandbox/public_token/create'"
  transport: json
  body:
    client_id: "{{ credentials.plaidCredential.clientId }}"
    secret: "{{ credentials.plaidCredential.secret }}"
    # DEFAULTS APPLIED HERE, not left to the schema, because that is where the existing service applied
    # them — its signature defaulted institutionId, testUsername and testPassword, so an empty config
    # still produced a working call. As plain `{{ }}` templates an unset value is OMITTED (the resolver
    # drops a key that resolved to ""), and Plaid REQUIRES institution_id: the request would fail with
    # a missing-field error that named the config field nobody had to fill in. Making them `required`
    # instead would break every saved workflow that relied on the old defaults.
    institution_id: "return config.institutionId || 'ins_109508'"
    initial_products: ["transactions"]
    options:
      override_username: "return config.testUsername || 'user_transactions_dynamic'"
      override_password: "return config.testPassword || 'pass_good'"
  # Plaid answers 400 WITH a JSON body naming the reason, so the body is what to read.
  error:
    when: "return !!response.error_code"
    message: "return response.error_message || response.error_code"

- name: access
  method: POST
  url: "return 'https://' + (credentials.plaidCredential.environment || 'sandbox') + '.plaid.com/item/public_token/exchange'"
  transport: json
  body:
    client_id: "{{ credentials.plaidCredential.clientId }}"
    secret: "{{ credentials.plaidCredential.secret }}"
    # The previous call's reply, by its name. This is the whole reason `run` is an ordered list.
    public_token: "{{ calls.login.public_token }}"
  error:
    when: "return !!response.error_code"
    message: "return response.error_message || response.error_code"

# THE ONLY CALL THAT FETCHES ANYTHING, and the one that has to wait.
#
# Plaid answers `PRODUCT_NOT_READY` when a freshly created item has no transaction history prepared
# yet — which is every run of this node, because it just invented the item. The existing TypeScript
# handled that with its own loop: five attempts, two seconds apart.
#
# THAT LOOP IS A POLL. "Send it again until the answer is ready" is the same shape as "ask the job
# until it is finished", so it is declared rather than reimplemented. It needs `poll.method: POST`
# with `poll.body` — the capability built for AWS Textract — and the status check here happens to be
# the SAME endpoint with the SAME body, which the generic poll supports without knowing that.
#
# `until` is tested against the FIRST reply before any waiting, so a ready item costs no extra call.
- name: transactions
  method: POST
  url: "return 'https://' + (credentials.plaidCredential.environment || 'sandbox') + '.plaid.com/transactions/get'"
  transport: json
  body:
    client_id: "{{ credentials.plaidCredential.clientId }}"
    secret: "{{ credentials.plaidCredential.secret }}"
    access_token: "{{ calls.access.access_token }}"
    # `Date.iso` formats what `Date.now()` could already read. Before it existed the sandbox could do
    # the arithmetic and had no way to render it, which is what made this node look unmigratable.
    start_date: "return Date.iso(Date.now() - (config.daysBack || 30) * 86400000).split('T')[0]"
    end_date: "return Date.iso().split('T')[0]"
    options:
      # Same reasoning as the login call: the existing service defaulted this to 100.
      count: "return config.maxTransactions || 100"
      offset: 0

  poll:
    # The same endpoint, re-sent. Not a status URL, because Plaid has none — readiness is reported by
    # the fetch itself.
    url: "return 'https://' + (credentials.plaidCredential.environment || 'sandbox') + '.plaid.com/transactions/get'"
    method: POST
    # `credentials` and `calls` are BOTH in scope here — a poll expression sees the whole run context
    # with the start reply layered on as `response` — so the body is rebuilt from the same sources
    # rather than smuggled through config.
    body: |
      return {
        client_id: credentials.plaidCredential.clientId,
        secret: credentials.plaidCredential.secret,
        access_token: calls.access.access_token,
        start_date: Date.iso(Date.now() - (config.daysBack || 30) * 86400000).split('T')[0],
        end_date: Date.iso().split('T')[0],
        options: { count: config.maxTransactions || 100, offset: 0 }
      };
    # Ready when Plaid stops saying "not ready".
    until: "return response.error_code !== 'PRODUCT_NOT_READY'"
    # Any OTHER error is a real failure, caught rather than waited on: re-sending a bad request just
    # sends the same bad request again, five times, and then reports a timeout instead of the reason.
    failed: "return !!response.error_code && response.error_code !== 'PRODUCT_NOT_READY'"
    message: "return response.error_message || response.error_code"
    # The existing node's own numbers: 2s apart, 5 attempts.
    intervalMs: 2000
    maxAttempts: 5
files.config.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/config.schema.json

# `useCache` and `cacheTTLMinutes` are GONE — see node.yaml for why. A saved workflow that set them
# will simply have two fields nothing reads, rather than failing.

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: []
  properties:
    testUsername:
      type: string
      title: Test Username
      description: >-
        Plaid Sandbox test username. user_transactions_dynamic gives the most realistic history;
        the others are fixed personas.
      default: user_transactions_dynamic
      enum: [user_transactions_dynamic, user_good, user_ewa_user, user_yuppie, user_small_business]
    testPassword:
      type: string
      title: Test Password
      description: Plaid Sandbox test password (any value works for most test users)
      default: pass_good
    institutionId:
      type: string
      title: Institution ID
      description: "Plaid institution ID. Default: First Platypus Bank (ins_109508), recommended for sandbox"
      default: ins_109508
    daysBack:
      type: number
      title: Days Back
      description: Number of days of transaction history to fetch
      default: 30
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 730
    maxTransactions:
      type: number
      title: Max Transactions
      description: Maximum number of transactions to return
      default: 100
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 500
"ui:order":
  [testUsername, testPassword, institutionId, daysBack, maxTransactions]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Trigger signal to start fetching transactions
    required: false

# THE NAMES ARE THE EXISTING NODE'S, unchanged, because a saved workflow references an output by name.
# `startDate` and `endDate` are kept for that reason even though they only echo back what the node
# computed: renaming or dropping them would silently empty a downstream template.
outputs:
  - name: transactions
    type: array
    description: Array of transaction objects
  - name: accounts
    type: array
    description: Array of account objects
  - name: totalTransactions
    type: number
    description: Total number of transactions available
  - name: startDate
    type: string
    description: Start date of the transaction range (YYYY-MM-DD)
  - name: endDate
    type: string
    description: End date of the transaction range (YYYY-MM-DD)

credentials:
  - name: plaidCredential
    required: true
files.node.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/node.schema.json

type: PlaidTransactions
kind: PromiseNode

name: Plaid Transactions
category: Storage & Data
color: "#00D09C"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1765729171/gravity/icons/plaid_logo.png

description: Fetch bank transactions from Plaid Sandbox for testing.

whenToUse: >-
  Pick ONLY when a workflow needs realistic test bank transactions. It hits Plaid Sandbox with test
  personas and never a live account, so it is a sandbox data source rather than a general store of
  real records.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NOT cacheable. The existing node had its OWN Redis cache — useCache and cacheTTLMinutes, keyed per
  # workflow — and both are DROPPED here rather than reimplemented, which is the one deliberate
  # behaviour change in this migration.
  #
  # Two reasons. The data is invented sandbox data, so re-fetching costs nothing anyone is paying for.
  # And the platform already has node memoization, gated on exactly this flag — a second, node-private
  # cache with its own TTL semantics is the kind of thing that later disagrees with the first.
  #
  # It stays FALSE rather than becoming true because each run mints a NEW sandbox item, so two runs
  # legitimately return different transactions and a shared answer would be wrong.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/test.schema.json

# The existing node's own fixture. Running it live needs INGEST_PLAID_CLIENT_ID and INGEST_PLAID_SECRET
# (or PLAID_CLIENT_ID / PLAID_SECRET) — sandbox keys, which is all this node can use.
#
# It reaches the real Plaid sandbox, so it exercises the whole chain: invent a login, exchange it, then
# poll until the freshly created item has history. That last part is the interesting one — a new item
# nearly always answers PRODUCT_NOT_READY at least once.

testData:
  config:
    testUsername: user_transactions_dynamic
    testPassword: pass_good
    institutionId: ins_109508
    daysBack: 30
    maxTransactions: 100
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    # An ARRAY, and one that actually has something in it: user_transactions_dynamic always returns
    # history, so an empty array means the poll gave up early rather than that the account is quiet.
    transactions: "return Array.isArray(output.transactions) && output.transactions.length > 0"
    accounts: "return Array.isArray(output.accounts) && output.accounts.length > 0"
    # YYYY-MM-DD, and the range the right way round. A sign error in the arithmetic would still produce
    # two valid-looking dates.
    startDate: "return /^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$/.test(output.startDate) && output.startDate < output.endDate"
